new_statements.translation: 2.4 Tone. In Brokkat a phonological opposition between high tone and low tone is recognised. In addition a rising tone is observed as a contour tone. As an allotone of the high tone, a falling tone appears at a morpheme boundary ([55] > [53] or [54] /__#). Suprasegmentals such as stress and phonation type are not distinctive in this language. [...] [p. 9:] In polysyllabic words, when the first syllable is high-toned the following syllables are low; when the first syllable is low-toned the second syllable becomes high and the third syllable is low.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Brokkat is described as a (Tibetic-type) tone language with a high/low register contrast (plus a rising contour) carried by the word; stress is explicitly stated not to be distinctive. Word-level pitch pattern is fixed by the first syllable's tone: H-L-L or L-H-L, i.e. a single pitch peak within the first two syllables. No statement of where phonetic prominence/stress falls.
new_statements.exceptions: Falling allotone of high tone before a morpheme boundary; rising tone also occurs phonetically on checked syllables but is not distinctive there (p. 8, summary point 4 p. 16). No stress exceptions discussed.
new_statements.domain_note: Statements concern the word (monosyllables in citation form for tone; explicit rule for polysyllabic words). Based on elicited lexical data from one 63-year-old native speaker of Dhur village, fieldwork 2013-2014; author calls it a preliminary report.
new_statements.identity_note: Nishida 2014 describes the Brokkat (Brokpa-gi-kha, 'B'umthang D'urg'i Bjobikha') of Dhur/Dur village, Chokhor valley, Bumthang district, central Bhutan — exactly Glottolog brok1249 'Dur Brokkat' (ISO bro); not to be confused with Mera-Sakteng Brokpa-ke (sakt1234) of Trashigang. Data from a single 63-year-old speaker.

sources.locator: Section 2.4 トーン, p. 8 (stress/tone statement) and p. 9 (polysyllabic tone pattern); PDF pages 8-9
sources.note: Sec. 2.4 'Tone' (p. 8): phonemic high vs low tone plus a rising contour tone; falling allotone of high at morpheme boundary; 'suprasegmentals such as stress and phonation type are not distinctive in this language'. p. 9: polysyllabic words are H-L(-L) if first syllable high, L-H-L if first syllable low. Syllable template (C1)(C2)V(C3)/T (p. 6). Author states (p. 1) that no prior linguistic record of Brokkat existed.

Confirms the 2014 paper is Nishida's only published Brokkat description; related: Nishida 2011 'Pitch and tone in some Bhutanese languages' (pp. 29-36 in Tone, Accent and Intonation in Eastern Eurasian Languages) — not opened, coverage of Brokkat unknown (predates his 2013 Brokkat fieldwork, so unlikely).
